newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian union votes to end strike on Thursday - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russian union votes to end strike on Thursday - Tass.

text.p: A Russian coal miners' union has decided to end from Thursday a nationwide strike it began on December 3 to back demands for payment of wage arrears, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass said the decision to resume work at pits and open cast mines on Thursday had been taken at a meeting of the Rosugleprof union's leadership late on Wednesday after the government had agreed to meet some of the miners' demands.
It quoted a protocol of Rosugleprof meeting as saying that among other things the government has promised to pay all wage arrears befor the end of the year.
Tass gave no details. Neither the union nor the government were available for comment.
Up to 400,000 miners in nearly 200 pits and open cast mines across Russia have taken part in the protest.
The union says goverment debt to the industry is worth around two trillion roubles ($400 million) and even greater company debts had led to huge delays in paying out wages.

At some mines the workers also demanded the resignation of the government and a dramatic change of the current course of economic reform. But the majority of strikers stopped short of making political demands.
The miners' strike has been used by communist opposition in the State Duma lower house of parliament to blast the government during crucial debates on the draft 1997 budget.
The chamber is expected to debate the draft again on Sunday.

Pro-democracy strikes by coal miners in 1989 and 1990 helped Russian President Boris Yeltsin in his struggle against the communist administration which ended with the collapse of the Soviet Union in late 1991.
But bold market reforms launched by Yeltsin after the victory turned out to be damaging for the mines, most of which are loss-making.
Since the start of reconstruction in the coal sector in 1993, the government has closed 50 unprofitable mines and says it plans to shut more than 60 others soon.
